batter.definition: n. (baseball) a ballplayer who is batting\nn. a liquid or semiliquid mixture, as of flour, eggs, and milk, used in cooking
batter.translation: v. 连续猛打（尤其指妇女），猛击\nn. 面糊（食物），击球员，打击手

examples.en: To be a good batter, you've got to hang loose and follow your instincts.
examples.zh: 想成为一个好的击球手的话，你要在球场上时刻保持镇定，还要学会相信自己的直觉。

examples.en: Tom's daughter pretended not to know him when he came to pick her up from school in his battered old car.
examples.zh: 当汤姆开着他破旧的雷泽车来接女儿放学时，他的女儿假装不认识他。

beautify.definition: v make more beautiful\nv be beautiful to look at\nv make more attractive by adding ornament, colour, etc.
beautify.translation: vt. 美化, 变美, 修饰

examples.en: We use them to beautify our home.
The Blessed are beautified, the saints are sanctified and rats are ratified.
Hundreds of years ago, married Japanese women would blacken their teeth to beautify themselves.

belongings.definition:
n something owned; any tangible or intangible possession that is owned by someone; 
n happiness felt in a secure relationship
v be owned by; be in the possession of
v be suitable or acceptable
v be in the right place or situation
v be rightly classified in a class or category
v be a member, adherent, inhabitant, etc. (of a group, organization, or place)
v be a part or adjunct
belongings.translation: n. 财产, 所有物, 相关事物\n[经] 财产, 所有物, 附属物

examples.en: Please do not forget your belongings.
examples.zh: 请勿望您的物品。

examples.en: Are these all your belongings?
examples.zh: 这些东西全都是你的吗？

examples.en: Brian left his belongings behind.
examples.zh: Brian 丢下了自己的财产。

beneficiary.definition: n. the recipient of funds or other benefits\na. having or arising from a benefice
beneficiary.translation: n. 受惠者, 受益人\na. 受封的

examples.en: Can I write the name of the beneficiary in Russian?
Sami rewrote his will, adding Layla as a major beneficiary.
Sami changed the beneficiary of his life insurance to Layla.

benevolence.definition: n. disposition to do good\nn. an inclination to do kind or charitable acts\nn. an act intending or showing kindness and good will
benevolence.translation: n. 善意, 慈悲, 善行\n[法] 捐助物, 捐款, 仁慈

examples.en: Deep inside your heart, nurture benevolence for everything that exists!
A certain hallmark of wisdom is the cheerful benevolence it confers.
Benevolence is abstract, a good deed is concrete.

besiege.definition: v. surround so as to force to give up\nv. cause to feel distressed or worried\nv. harass, as with questions or requests

examples.en: The author of Fortress Besieged is Qian Zhongshu.
examples.zh: 《围城》的作者是钱钟书。

beware.definition: v. be on one's guard; be cautious or wary about; be alert to

examples.en: Beware of anyone who claims objectivity.
examples.zh: 要小心那些说自己客观的人。

examples.en: Beware of anybody who claims objectivity.
examples.zh: 要小心那些说自己客观的人。

examples.en: You should beware of overconfidence.
examples.zh: 你要注意不要太自信。

bilateral.definition: s. having identical parts on each side of an axis\ns. affecting or undertaken by two parties\ns. having two sides or parts
bilateral.translation: a. 有两边的, 双边的, 双方的\n[医] 两侧的

examples.en: That is, bilateral trade is now in favor of Bangladesh.
Algeria and Russia have a growing rise in bilateral trade.
The doctors announced a diagnosis of advanced bilateral pneumonia.

billionaire.definition: n. a very rich person whose material wealth is valued at more than a billion dollars

examples.en: I always dreamed of being a billionaire.
examples.zh: 我总是梦想著成为亿万富翁。

binoculars.definition: n. an optical instrument designed for simultaneous use by both eyes
binoculars.translation: n. 双目镜, 双筒镜\n[机] 双目镜

examples.en: Lend me the binoculars so I can see it better.
Do you have a pair of binoculars I could borrow?
Tom refused to tell me who gave him those binoculars.

biochemical.definition: a. of or relating to biochemistry; involving chemical processes in living organisms
biochemical.translation: a. 生物化学的\n[机] 生物化学的

examples.en: Is the coronavirus really a biochemical weapon?
Edmundo was an Algerian biochemical engineer.
Sami studied biochemical engineering.

biochemist.definition: n. someone with special training in biochemistry

examples.en: I'm a biochemist, though I lack work experience.
Tom hopes to be a biochemist someday.
A biochemist gathers mutants for everything as if they were ingredients for a recipe.

biographer.definition: n. someone who writes an account of a person's life

examples.en: Yanni and Rima's relationship intrigued biographers and historians for years.
His biographer called him a wonderful man.
Tom is a biographer.

biotechnology.definition: n. the branch of molecular biology that studies the use of microorganisms to perform specific industrial processes\nn. the branch of engineering science in which biological science is used to study the relation between workers and their environments
biotechnology.translation: n. 生物工艺学；生物技术

examples.en: It's very easy to drink potato shochu now that the potato-like smell has been reduced to a low level through use of the latest biotechnology.
examples.zh: 透过现今的生物科技，蕃薯烧酒已经变得十分容易入口了，因为那种难闻的蕃薯味道大部分已经被去除了。

blackmail.definition: n. extortion of money by threats to divulge discrediting information\nv. exert pressure on someone through threats\nv. obtain through threats

examples.en: The victim of blackmail has been paying hush money for years, but now he realizes it is foolish, and has decided not to pay a red cent more.
examples.zh: 被害人被勒索支付封口费已经很多年, 但现在他意识到这样做是愚蠢的, 而且他已经决定再也不付一毛钱了。

blond.definition: n. a person with fair skin and hair\nn. a light grayish yellow to near white\na. being or having light colored skin and hair and usually blue or grey eyes
blond.translation: a. 金发的\nn. 白肤碧眼金发的人

examples.en: Mary is in love with the boy with blond hair.
Sami's mother was bleaching his hair blond to match hers.
He isn't a blond prince but I love him.

blush.definition: n. sudden reddening of the face (as from embarrassment or guilt or shame or modesty)\nv. turn red, as if in embarrassment or shame\nv. become rosy or reddish
blush.translation: vi. 脸红, 羞愧\nvt. 弄成红色\nn. 脸红

examples.en: Bob is very timid and blushes when chatting with girls.
examples.zh: 鲍伯非常胆小，和女生聊天时会脸红。

examples.en: The man blushed like a boy.
examples.zh: 男人的脸像小孩般红了起来。

examples.en: He saw her and blushed.
examples.zh: 他看到她就脸红了。

boiler.definition: n. sealed vessel where water is converted to steam
boiler.translation: n. 煮器, 汽锅, 锅炉\n[化] 锅炉

examples.en: Give me a reading on that meter near the boiler.
I forgot to turn on the boiler before taking a shower.
The door to the boiler room was opened.

bowel.definition: n the part of the alimentary canal between the stomach and the anus
bowel.translation: n. 肠, 内脏, 内部\nvt. 挖...的内脏

examples.en: I have not had a bowel movement for a week.
Frequent bowel movements are a common occurrence for me.
I bleed when I have bowel movements.

brag.definition: n. an instance of boastful talk

examples.en: The difference between bragging and being ambitious is miniscule.
examples.zh: 吹嘘与雄心的差别甚小。

examples.en: I don't mean to brag.
examples.zh: 我不想吹牛。

examples.en: He bragged about the killing.
examples.zh: 他吹嘘这场谋杀。

bravery.definition: n a quality of spirit that enables you to face danger or pain without showing fear\nn feeling no fear

examples.en: Ancient people liked to tell stories of bravery.
examples.zh: 古人喜欢讲关于勇气的故事。

examples.en: Today I finally worked up the bravery to say to her "I love you!"
examples.zh: 今天我终于鼓起勇气对她说：“我爱你！”。

examples.en: Four brave military dogs were awarded the K-9 Medal of Courage for their bravery and service.
examples.zh: 四只英勇的军犬因其勇气与贡献获颁 K-9 勇气勋章。

brewery.definition: n. a plant where beer is brewed by fermentation
brewery.translation: n. 啤酒厂, 酿酒厂\n[经] 酿造所

examples.en: The theft took place in front of the brewery.
He couldn't organize a piss-up in a brewery.
You couldn't organise a piss-up in a brewery!

bribery.definition: n. the practice of offering something (usually money) in order to gain an illicit advantage
bribery.translation: n. 贿赂行为, 行贿, 受贿\n[经] 行贿, 受贿

examples.en: The government's anti-corruption tsar resigned yesterday following allegations of bribery.
Sympathy, for me, is the only form of bribery.
Between you and me, he was dismissed for bribery.

bridegroom.definition: n a man who has recently been married\nn a man participant in his own marriage ceremony

examples.en: Matthew is soon to be married; he will make a very handsome bridegroom.
My bridegroom cheated on me.
He is the bridegroom.

briefing.definition: n. detailed instructions, as for a military operation
briefing.translation: n. 简报\n[法] 简报, 情况的简要介绍

examples.en: Putin was briefing his generals about an upcoming war.
Dan interrupted Linda's briefing saying that the building was on fire.
Tom needs you in the briefing room.

brigade.definition: n. army unit smaller than a division\nv. form or unite into a brigade
brigade.translation: n. 旅, 队\n[法] 团体, 队, 组

examples.en: Would you call the fire brigade to save an ant?
The fire brigade had to go out twice this evening.
The fire brigade arrived to find the house well alight.

brilliance.translation: n. 卓越, 光辉\n[电] 辉度

examples.en: His brilliance has taken him quite some places in life.
Every time I saw him, I was overcome with his brilliance.
Russian ballet is world-renowned for its technical brilliance, artistry, and beauty.

broke.translation: a. 一文不名的\nbreak的过去式

examples.en: I know you were the one who broke the window.
examples.zh: 我知道窗户是你打烂的。

examples.en: Adam was furious with me when I broke his watch.
examples.zh: 我把亚当的手表弄坏了，气得他七窍生烟。

examples.en: My brother fell from the tree and broke his leg.
examples.zh: 我的弟弟(或者哥哥)从树上掉下来摔断了腿。

brow.definition: n. the part of the face above the eyes
brow.translation: n. 眉毛, 额\n[医] 额, 眉, 睫毛

examples.en: The sweat was dripping off my brow.
examples.zh: 汗水从我的额头上落下。

examples.en: On hearing that, he knitted his brow.
examples.zh: 他听到那个时，皱起了眉头。

examples.en: Wipe the sweat from your brow.
examples.zh: 擦掉你额头上的汗。

buck.definition:
n. United States author whose novels drew on her experiences as a missionary in China (1892-1973)
n. mature male of various mammals (especially deer or antelope)
v. to strive with determination
v. resist
buck.translation:
n. 元, 雄鹿, 纨绔子弟, 鞍马, 培克(赌博时的庄家标志), 碱水, 自夸, 谈话
vi. 马背突然拱起, 反对, 吹牛, 闲聊
vt. 马背突然拱起将骑手摔下, 反对, 用碱水洗
a. 雄的

examples.en: Where is your twenty? I'll give you five bucks for it.
examples.zh: 你的二十块在哪里? 我给你五块钱找到它。

examples.en: He borrowed one hundred bucks from me.
examples.zh: 他跟我借一百块。

examples.en: I'm tracking a buck.
examples.zh: 我正在追踪一头公鹿。

budgetary.definition: a. of or relating to a budget
budgetary.translation: a. 预算的\n[法] 预算的

examples.en: Algeria needs budgetary stability.

bumper.definition: n. a glass filled to the brim (especially as a toast)\nn. a mechanical device consisting of bars at either end of a vehicle to absorb shock and prevent serious damage
bumper.translation: n. 缓冲器, 满杯\na. 大胜利的

examples.en: Adriano wanted to go on the bumper car ride.
Benedito and his friends will ride the bumper cars.
Benedito will ride the bumper boats with his family.

bureaucrat.definition: n. an official of a bureaucracy
bureaucrat.translation: n. 官僚作风的人, 官僚, 官僚主义者\n[法] 官僚, 官僚作风的人

examples.en: In Algeria, almost everything is controlled by bureaucrats and politicians.
Bureaucrats are testing the waters over revising old regulations.
The bureaucrats maintain solid ties with the gigantic corporations.

bureaucratic.definition: a. of or relating to or resembling a bureaucrat or bureaucracy
bureaucratic.translation: a. 官僚的\n[经] 机僚化的

examples.en: I hope we don't run into any bureaucratic red tape.
In fact, this is a major means of bureaucratic control.
Algeria needs to put an end to the bureaucratic headache.

burglar.definition: n. a thief who enters a building with intent to steal
burglar.translation: n. 窃贼\n[法] 夜盗, 窃贼, 盗窃者

examples.en: The burglar gained access to the house through this door.
examples.zh: 窃贼是从这扇门进到屋子里的。

examples.en: The police think the burglar entered through a basement window.
examples.zh: 警察认为窃贼从地下室窗口进入。

examples.en: It seems that the burglar broke in through an upstairs window.
examples.zh: 强盗似乎是在上层破窗而入的。

burglary.definition: n. entering a building unlawfully with intent to commit a felony or to steal valuable property
burglary.translation: n. 夜盗行为, 盗窃, 盗窃行为\n[法] 夜盗行为, 夜间入屋窃盗罪, 窃盗

examples.en: The inmate was doing time for a burglary conviction.
Documents relating to his private life were stolen in the burglary.
He was arrested on the charge of burglary.

butt.definition:
n. thick end of the handle
n. the part of a plant from which the roots spring or the part of a stalk or trunk nearest the roots
n. a victim of ridicule or pranks
n. a large cask (especially one holding a volume equivalent to 2 hogsheads or 126 gallons)
butt.translation: n. 粗大的一头, 烟头, 靶, 笑柄\n[医] 对核

examples.en: Mr. Goat Butt never told me there would be a partner.
examples.zh: 羊屁股先生可没告诉我还有搭档。

examples.en: Don't throw cigarette butts on the ground. Cockroaches might get cancer.
examples.zh: 别把烟头往地上扔，要不然蟑螂会得癌症的。

examples.en: She has a big butt.
examples.zh: 她的屁股很大。

bystander.translation: n. 旁观者, 目击者\n[法] 候补陪审员, 旁观者

examples.en: A bystander videotaped the police beating using their cell phone.
The incident happened to be captured on video by a bystander.
Bystanders should be trained in safe rescue and resuscitation.

backfire.definition:
n. a loud noise made by the explosion of fuel in the manifold or exhaust of an internal combustion engine
n. a fire that is set intentionally in order to slow an approaching forest fire or grassfire by clearing a burned area in its path
n. a miscalculation that recoils on its maker
v. come back to the originator of an action with an undesired effect
backfire.translation: n. 逆火, 回火, 放火\nvi. 放逆火, 预先放火, 发生意外

examples.en: Are you sure this won't backfire on us?
Tom thought that he heard a car backfire.
He thought he heard a car backfire.

believer.definition: n. a supporter who accepts something as true\nn. a person who has religious faith

examples.en: I don't like false believers.
examples.zh: 我不喜欢虚伪的信徒。

best-seller.translation: n. 畅销书或唱片; 畅销书作者

examples.en: His new novel has become a best-seller.
The Bible is a best-seller book.
Tom's book became an instant best-seller.

bloc.definition: n. a group of countries in special alliance

examples.en: Those agenda items were taken up en bloc for discussion.
Indigeneity only matters selectively to the so-called "anti-imperialist" bloc.
India and China are two BRIC bloc countries.

blockade.definition:
n. a war measure that isolates some area of importance to the enemy
n. prevents access or progress
v. obstruct access to
v. impose a blockade on

examples.en: I am not hindered by the blockade on the street.
A blockade can be a legitimate tool in a democracy.
In front of the embassy, there was a large blockade.

bacterium.definition: n (microbiology) single-celled or noncellular spherical or spiral or rod-shaped organisms lacking chlorophyll that reproduce by fission; important as pathogens and for biochemical properties; taxonomy is difficult; often considered to be plants
bacterium.translation: n. 细菌\n[医] [无芽胞]杆菌属

examples.en: Do not confuse a virus with a bacterium.
This bacterium is resistant to penicillin.
Koalas face many threats, including chlamydia – a bacterium that can cause pneumonia and infertility.

badminton.definition: n. a game played on a court with light long-handled rackets used to volley a shuttlecock over a net

examples.en: I used to play badminton a lot, but I don’t play anymore.
examples.zh: 我以前常去打羽毛球，但现在不打了。

examples.en: He plays badminton very well.
examples.zh: 他的羽毛球打得真厉害。

examples.en: They play badminton here often.
examples.zh: 他们常在这儿打羽毛球。

bandit.definition: n. an armed thief who is (usually) a member of a band

examples.en: The bandits ran away when they heard the police siren.
With their employer dead, the mercenaries soon turned into bandits.
He threw the bandit off his horse.

banker.definition: n. a financier who owns or is an executive in a bank\nn. the person in charge of the bank in a gambling game
banker.translation: n. 银行家, 庄家\n[经] 银行业者, 银行家

examples.en: I want to be a banker when I grow up.
Tom wants to be a banker when he grows up.
I thought that you said that Tom was a banker.

barber.definition: n. United States composer (1910-1981)\nn. a hairdresser who cuts hair and shaves beards as a trade\nv. perform the services of a barber: cut the hair and/or beard of

examples.en: I had my hair cut at the barber shop yesterday.
examples.zh: 我昨天去了理发店理发。

examples.en: A barber is a man who shaves and cuts men's hair.
examples.zh: 理发师是为男人刮胡子和剪头发的人。

examples.en: I want to go to the barber.
examples.zh: 我要去理发了。

beggar.definition: n. a pauper who lives by begging\nv. be beyond the resources of\nv. reduce to beggary
beggar.translation: n. 乞丐\nvt. 使贫穷, 使成乞丐

examples.en: He is rich yet he lives like a beggar.
examples.zh: 他很富有，但活得像个乞丐。

examples.en: I gave the beggar all the money I had.
examples.zh: 我把身上的钱全都给了那个乞丐。

examples.en: I gave the beggar what money I had.
examples.zh: 我把身上的钱全都给了那个乞丐。

beginner.definition: n someone new to a field or activity\nn a person who founds or establishes some institution

examples.en: Tom's a beginner, but he catches on fast.
examples.zh: 汤姆是个初学者，但他赶上得很快。

examples.en: You are a good tennis player, as beginners go.
examples.zh: 以初学者来说，你打网球已经算是打得不错了。

examples.en: When learning Chinese, pinyin is very helpful for beginners.
examples.zh: 学习汉语的时候，拼音对初学者很有帮助。

biased.definition: s. favoring one person or side over another
biased.translation: a. 有偏见的\n[计] 边缘的

examples.en: Concerning this issue, I feel that the trash media only report biased information.
examples.zh: 关于这个问题，我觉得垃圾媒体只报道了很片面的信息。

biotech.definition: n the branch of molecular biology that studies the use of microorganisms to perform specific industrial processes

examples.en: Sami was a business manager at a biotech company.
Biotech and Moderna have a lead in the Corona or Covid vaccination.
Martino is an Algerian biotech engineer.

bitterly.definition: r. with bitterness, in a resentful manner\nr. indicating something hard to accept
bitterly.translation: adv. 怨恨地, 悲痛地, 残酷地

examples.en: Nakamatsu smiled bitterly at his own stupid question.
examples.zh: 中松为自己的愚蠢问题苦笑。

bitterness.definition: n. a rough and bitter manner\nn. the property of having a harsh unpleasant taste
bitterness.translation: n. 苦味, 悲痛, 怨恨

examples.en: He couldn't stand the bitterness of the coffee.
examples.zh: 他受不了咖啡的苦味。

examples.en: She said good-bye with a smile, but there was a good deal of bitterness in her heart.
examples.zh: 她说再见的时候，脸上挂著笑容，但其实心中是十分难受的。

blacksmith.definition: n. a smith who forges and shapes iron with a hammer and anvil

examples.en: It's by smithing that one becomes a blacksmith.
examples.zh: 打铁成铁匠。

bluntly.definition: r in a blunt direct manner
bluntly.translation: adv. 坦率地, 率直地

examples.en: To put it bluntly, he's mistaken.
examples.zh: 坦率地说，他错了。

examples.en: Mary bluntly rejected Tom's request.
examples.zh: 玛丽直截了当地拒绝了汤姆的请求。

bosom.definition:
n. the chest considered as the place where secret thoughts are kept
n. a person's breast or chest
n. cloth that covers the chest or breasts
v. hide in one's bosom
bosom.translation: n. 胸部, 胸, 胸怀, 内部, 中间\nvt. 怀抱

examples.en: He was happy in the bosom of his family.
What a viper I have nourished in my bosom!
Tom and Mary have been bosom friends for years.

bough.definition: n. any of the larger branches of a tree

examples.en: The boughs that bear most hang lowest.
examples.zh: 稻穗越饱满越低头。

bourgeois.definition:
n. a member of the middle class
s. (according to Marxist thought) being of the property-owning class and exploitive of the working class
s. conforming to the standards and conventions of the middle class
s. belonging to the middle class
bourgeois.translation: n. 中产阶级分子, 商人, 资产阶级\na. 中产阶级的, 平庸的\nn. 九点活字

examples.en: Of course, walking away from the bourgeois scene wasn't easy.
Truly, never before has bourgeois sociology known such a fall!
The idealism of American bourgeois philosophers is aggressive and warlike.

brandy.definition: n. distilled from wine or fermented fruit juice
brandy.translation: n. 白兰地酒\n[化] 白兰地

examples.en: She poured brandy into the glasses.
examples.zh: 她把白兰地倒进玻璃杯里。

examples.en: The Spanish make a type of brandy with the fruits of the strawberry tree.
examples.zh: 西班牙人用草莓树的果实酿造一种白兰地。

bridle.definition:
n. headgear for a horse; includes a headstall and bit and reins to give the rider or driver control
n. the act of restraining power or action or limiting excess
v. anger or take offense
v. put a bridle on
bridle.translation: n. 马勒, 约束\n[医] 系带, 约束

examples.en: Oleg never put a bridle or a saddle on that horse.
He threw the bridle over the fence and strode up the pathway.
Fine markings around the muzzle and shoulder hint at an early bridle.

brighten.translation: vi. 变亮, 活跃\nvt. 使生辉, 使快活

examples.en: He was painting the walls to brighten up the room.
We painted the walls white to brighten up the room.
Ziri chose a colorful birdhouse to brighten up the garden.

brightness.definition: n. the location of a visual perception along a continuum from black to white\nn. intelligence as manifested in being quick and witty
brightness.translation: n. 光亮, 明亮, 聪明\n[计] 亮度

examples.en: The brightness of her smile always makes me feel better.
We perceive the amplitude of a light wave as brightness.
He flipped the switch and threw the room into brightness.

broken.definition:
a. physically and forcibly separated into pieces or cracked or split
a. not continuous in space, time, or sequence or varying abruptly
s. subdued or brought low in condition or status
a. (especially of promises or contracts) having been violated or disregarded
broken.translation: a. 坏掉的, 打破的, 断掉的\nbreak的过去分词

examples.en: I can't turn it on, because the switch is broken.
examples.zh: 因为开关坏了，我没法儿把它打开。

examples.en: He got a broken jaw and lost some teeth.
examples.zh: 他磕碎了下巴，掉了几颗牙。

examples.en: Even a broken clock is right twice a day.
examples.zh: 凡人皆有得意时。

brook.definition: n. a natural stream of water smaller than a river (and often a tributary of a river)

examples.en: The murmur of the brook lulls me to sleep.
examples.zh: 溪流潺潺，催我入眠。

bugle.definition: n. a brass instrument without valves; used for military calls and fanfares\nn. any of various low-growing annual or perennial evergreen herbs native to Eurasia; used for ground cover\nn. a tubular glass or plastic bead sewn onto clothing for decoration
bugle.translation: n. 喇叭, 号角\nv. 吹号

examples.en: Tom is trying to learn how to play the bugle.
Tom played Reveille on his bugle every morning.
Tom is learning to play the bugle.

bull.definition:
n. uncastrated adult male of domestic cattle
n. a large and strong and heavyset man
n. a serious and ludicrous blunder
n. uncomplimentary terms for a policeman
bull.translation: n. 公牛\n[法] 买方, 买空者

examples.en: He likes to throw the bull.
examples.zh: 他喜欢吹牛。

burner.definition: n. an apparatus for burning fuel (or refuse)\nn. the heating elements of a stove or range on which pots and pans are placed for cooking
burner.translation: n. 火炉, 烧火的人\n[化] 灯; 灯头; 烧嘴炉; 燃烧器; 燃烧炉

examples.en: Potassium, heated with a Bunsen burner, gives the flame a lilac color.
examples.zh: 用本生灯加热钾，火焰就会呈现淡紫色。

bushel.definition: n. a United States dry measure equal to 4 pecks or 2152.42 cubic inches\nn. a British imperial capacity measure (liquid or dry) equal to 4 pecks
bushel.translation: n. 蒲式耳(容量单位)\nv. 修整(衣物)

examples.en: Hide not your light under a bushel.
examples.zh: 不要把你的灯藏在斗笠下。

butcher.definition:
n. a retailer of meat
n. a brutal indiscriminate murderer
n. a person who slaughters or dresses meat for market
v. kill (animals) usually for food consumption
butcher.translation: n. 屠夫, 肉商, 小贩\nvt. 屠宰, 屠杀

examples.en: The butcher knife is in the drawer.
examples.zh: 屠夫的刀子在抽屉里。

examples.en: But the butcher is observing the holiday today, there's nothing we can do about it.
examples.zh: 可是肉店今天公休没办法。

by-product.definition: n. a secondary and sometimes unexpected consequence\nn. a product made during the manufacture of something else
by-product.translation: n. 副产品, 额外收获, 意外收获\n[计] 副产品

examples.en: Happiness is not a goal. It's a by-product of a life well lived.
Vegans do not use animal products, or by-products, in their everyday lives.
Cattle, such as dairy cows or beef cattle produce methane as a by-product of digestion.
